clue.text: Cameron, gathering backbench support, has a brief moment of calm

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: David Cameron was Prime Minister, abbreviated PM
the back of bench is its last letter
a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: David Cameron, propped up by his backbenchers, enjoys a short spell of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backbench' suggests MPs on the rear benches, but it means the back of the word bench. 'Moment of calm' looks like one phrase; 'of' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmatic person is unexcitable and composed, a synonym for calm in temperament.

clue.text: Prepared canapé wrapping gutted trout in bacon

indicators.note: the reworked letters wrap around the other piece
prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked
gutted means the inside is removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of trout

explanation.surface: A canapé is made by wrapping a cleaned trout in bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a recipe, but 'bacon' at the end is the definition, and the accent on canapé is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta is Italian cured pork belly, a kind of bacon.

clue.text: Remained decorous in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as the word is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like this one

parts.note: decorous means staid, sober and proper

explanation.surface: Someone kept polite in the way they talked.
explanation.walkthrough: Staid and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained in place, a simple past-tense synonym.

clue.text: In fact no student's put up a tent

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top
'no' means without, so the following item is taken away

parts.note: truly means in fact
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: It turns out no student pitched a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: TRULY without L gives TRUY, which is then written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A yurt is a round felt tent used by nomads in Central Asia.

clue.text: Twisted rambling vine round new helter-skelter tower

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first scrambled piece goes around the second
a rambling plant sprawls in all directions, so the letters spread into a new order
helter-skelter means in chaotic disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A climbing plant winds its way around a spiral fairground slide.
explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is a spiral fairground slide in the form of a tower, the picture the surface uses; here the word only signals disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Interwoven means twined together, so strands that are twisted around each other.

clue.text: Lobby for Conservative politician to capture a potential gain

indicators.note: the politician pieces capture the a between them

parts.note: MP is a member of parliament

indicators.note: potential means the letters of gain have possible other orders

explanation.surface: A Tory MP is pushed to seize a possible electoral gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby for' is a verb phrase, matching the verb sense of the answer rather than a noun for an electoral drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To campaign for something is to press or agitate for it, as a lobbyist does.

clue.text: Bewilder with live rock band?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
Muse is an English rock band

explanation.surface: Being puzzled by a live rock band's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'live rock band' reads as one concert but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse someone is to confuse or puzzle them, a synonym of bewilder.

clue.text: Joint for Ken and Barbie finally cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of Barbie

explanation.surface: Making a joint for Ken and Barbie dolls, which got cooked in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Listen! Consumption before vigorous run gives indigestion

indicators.note: before means the earlier pieces precede the last one

parts.note: to hear is to listen
TB, tuberculosis, was once called consumption

indicators.note: vigorous means the letters of run are shaken up

explanation.surface: A shout to pay attention: eating before a hard run brings on indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumption' looks like eating; it is the old name for tuberculosis, TB. RUN rearranged gives URN.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain in the chest caused by acid indigestion.

clue.text: A number, I included, dined at home

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something included is placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ten is a number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A count of diners, me included, who ate at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is the idiom for having a meal at home rather than out.

clue.text: Scramble record containing name and call time

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the next pieces go within the first

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
N is the abbreviation for name
a cry is a call
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Instructions for messing up a recording, adding a name and the time of a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the definition. An EP is an extended-play record, a short release.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a message is to encode it so outsiders cannot read it, which is to encrypt it.

clue.text: Support earth on steep banks leading to great river

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of steep
the Great Ouse is a river in eastern England

explanation.surface: Shoring up soil on the steep banks that lead down to a big river.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to support or adopt it.

clue.text: Toned down letter to Telegraph's head editor

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Telegraph
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A letter to a newspaper's chief editor was softened before printing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a British daily paper, so 'head editor' reads naturally, but 'head' belongs to Telegraph's.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted colours or voices are subdued, a synonym of toned down.

clue.text: Sailor returns to ship after day involved in alcohol and ribaldry

indicators.note: after puts the ship at the end, following the day-and-alcohol piece
returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: wine is alcohol
D is the abbreviation for day
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor returns to his ship after a day of drink and bawdy fun.
explanation.walkthrough: An able seaman is abbreviated AB, a standard crossword sailor; the steamship prefix supplies the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawdiness is coarse, sexual humour, the same thing as ribaldry.

clue.text: Older sibling keeping an eye on us?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a male sibling born earlier
second meaning: the all-seeing ruler of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, a byword for state surveillance

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, playful meaning: the watching leader on Orwell's posters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a brother older than you and the surveillance state figure from Orwell's novel.

clue.text: Broadcaster Larry King has lines cut when messing around

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcaster

indicators.note: cut means removed, so these letters are taken out of the name

parts.note: taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines

explanation.surface: The American chat-show host Larry King, his script trimmed, is fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines means railway lines, abbreviated RY; Sky is a British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarking is playing pranks or fooling about, the same as messing around.

clue.text: Shows gratitude to soldier with French wine, good time and celebration

parts.note: to thank is to show gratitude
a GI is an American soldier
vin is French for wine
G is the abbreviation for good
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Thanking a soldier with wine and a good time at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanksgiving Day is the American and Canadian autumn holiday, an annual celebration.

clue.text: Family has thousands, including rare florins King chucked out

indicators.note: the thousands surround the other piece

parts.note: K is a thousand, so two Ks are thousands

indicators.note: rare means unusual, so the letters of florins are rearranged
chucked out means the king's letter is thrown away from the fodder

parts.note: R is for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A household owns thousands, including rare coins a king threw away.
explanation.walkthrough: A florin was an old British two-shilling coin. R stands for Rex, Latin for king.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinsfolk are one's relatives, the members of one's family.

clue.text: Pronounce contract with mine's falling apart

indicators.note: to contract is to shrink, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to decree is to pronounce officially
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A mining contract is declared to be crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounce' looks like a sound signal and 'contract' like a legal document; in fact one is a verb of decreeing and the other a shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decrepit is worn out and dilapidated, in a state of falling apart.

clue.text: Make a break for it, when copper on beat's briefly tipsy

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: drunk means tipsy

explanation.surface: A suspect seizes their chance while a policeman on patrol is a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman and 'beat' like his patrol route; DRUNK loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut and run is the idiom for leaving hurriedly, making a quick escape.

clue.text: Makes fun of Great Aunt Sally's stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing is what lies inside, so the answer sits within the words that follow

parts.note: found running through these words

explanation.surface: Mocking a great aunt's cooking of the stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is also a British pub game of throwing sticks at a dummy, hence a target of ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to jeer at them, which is to make fun of them.

clue.text: Nightcap by Chanel's second hand

parts.note: Coco Chanel was the French fashion designer

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the next word

parts.note: the second letter of hand

explanation.surface: A bedtime drink from a second-hand Chanel shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second hand' reads as used goods, but 'second' picks one letter from hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink taken before bed, and cocoa is a classic example.

clue.text: Incentive for vehicle to get up hill

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Something that motivates a car to climb a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward dangled as an incentive, from the image of luring a donkey.

clue.text: Die from seizure after son's joke backfired

indicators.note: after sends the seizure to the end, following the son's joke

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: something that backfires comes back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: fun is a joke, as in 'in fun'
a fit is a seizure

explanation.surface: A father dies of a seizure when his son's prank goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The seizure goes 'after' the other pieces, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff it is informal British slang for to die.

clue.text: Add a small amount of money to pool

parts.note: to sum is to add up
P is a penny, a small coin in British money

explanation.surface: Contribute a few coins to a shared kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like a shared fund of money, but it is the definition for a reservoir of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or reservoir where liquid such as oil or water collects, a pool.

clue.text: Mad queen imprisoned in Berks improperly

indicators.note: imprisoned means locked inside, so one piece goes within the other
improperly means in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Berks rearranged
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A furious queen locked up in Berkshire without proper cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Berks is the abbreviation for Berkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Berserk means wild with rage, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Take first boyfriend to works' dances

indicators.note: taking the first means keeping only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter of boyfriend
ops is short for operations, works

explanation.surface: Bringing your first boyfriend to the office party dances.
explanation.definitionFit: Bops are informal dances or dance parties, used here as a plural noun.

clue.text: Student pursues bit of stuff to roadside lodging

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the student comes second

parts.note: a mote is a speck, a tiny bit of material
L is a learner, a student

explanation.surface: A student follows a girlfriend to a cheap roadside place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of stuff' is slang for an attractive woman, which is the surface trap; 'pursues' puts the student second.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a hotel for motorists, built beside a road.

clue.text: Sudden increase in time in which oxlips flourish

indicators.note: the rearranged flowers go in the time word

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time

indicators.note: flourish means the letters of oxlips are brandished into a new order

explanation.surface: A period when wild primulas suddenly bloom in abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' looks like the flowers thriving, but it signals the rearrangement. Oxlips are primrose-like wildflowers.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosion can mean a rapid surge in numbers, as in a population explosion.
